summary: Even as Eve is a 1920 American silent drama film produced by B. A. Rolfe and released by Associated First National Pictures, with A. H. Fischer Features as the producing company. Directed by Rolfe and Chester De Vonde, it was shot largely at the former Thanhouser Company studios in New Rochelle, New York, with some exteriors in the Adirondacks and on a Long Island estate. The film was based on Robert W. Chambers' short story "The Shining Band" and adapted by Charles Logue.
one_line: Even as Eve is a 1920 American silent drama film adapted from Robert W. Chambers' short story "The Shining Band".
key_facts: Even as Eve is a 1920 American silent drama film.
The film was made by A. H. Fischer Features and distributed by Associated First National Pictures.
B. A. Rolfe produced the film.
The film was directed by B. A. Rolfe and Chester De Vonde.
Arthur A. Cadwell and Conrad Wells (credited as A. Fried) served as cinematographers.
The film was filmed at the former Thanhouser Company studios in New Rochelle, New York.
Some exterior scenes were filmed in the New York Adirondack Mountains.
Some exterior scenes were filmed on a Long Island estate.
The film was based on the short story "The Shining Band" by Robert W. Chambers.
The screenplay was adapted by Charles Logue.
